\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{पदक} (padak)}{पदक (padak)}]{\mr{पदक} (padak) — a medal}

\label{lesson:MR-C530-padak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a playing field, then the Marathi for to overcome.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{पदक}}
\textbf{\mr{पदक}} — \emph{padak} — \textquotedblleft{}a medal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{स्पर्धेत} \mr{अरुणला} \mr{पदक} \mr{मिळालं}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{spardhet aruṇlā padak miḷālaṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Arun won a medal in the competition.
\end{quote}

Neuter.

\mr{सुवर्णपदक}, a gold medal.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{पदक}} (\emph{padak}) is a tatsama, taken from Sanskrit \emph{padaka}, a derivative of \emph{pada}, glossed as a kind of ornament (Monier-Williams); Marathi uses it for a medal.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{padak}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{padak}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{spardhet aruṇlā padak miḷālaṁ.} — Arun won a medal in the competition.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for a playing field, then the Marathi for to overcome, then say \emph{padak} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mr{पदक} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A medal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{चषक} (caṣak)}{चषक (caṣak)}]{\mr{चषक} (caṣak) — a trophy cup}

\label{lesson:MR-C530-casak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to overcome, then the Marathi for a medal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{चषक}}
\textbf{\mr{चषक}} — \emph{caṣak} — \textquotedblleft{}a trophy cup\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{जिंकलेल्या} \mr{संघाला} \mr{मोठा} \mr{चषक} \mr{मिळाला}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jiṅklelyā saṅghālā moṭhā caṣak miḷālā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The winning team got a big trophy.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{चषक}} (\emph{caṣak}) is a tatsama, taken from Sanskrit \emph{caṣaka}, \textquotedblleft{}a cup, a goblet\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{विक्रम} (vikram)}{विक्रम (vikram)}]{\mr{विक्रम} (vikram) — a sporting best; a record}

\label{lesson:MR-C530-vikram}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a medal, then the Marathi for a trophy cup.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{विक्रम}}
\textbf{\mr{विक्रम}} — \emph{vikram} — \textquotedblleft{}a sporting best; a record\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{तिने} \mr{धावण्यात} \mr{नवा} \mr{विक्रम} \mr{केला}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tine dhāvaṇyāt navā vikram kelā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She set a new record in running.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\mr{विक्रम} \mr{करणे}, to set a record; \mr{विक्रम} \mr{मोडणे}, to break one.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{विक्रम}} (\emph{vikram}) is a tatsama, taken from Sanskrit \emph{vikrama}, \textquotedblleft{}a stride, valour\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for a medal, then the Marathi for a trophy cup, then say \emph{vikram} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{स्पर्धक} (spardhak)}{स्पर्धक (spardhak)}]{\mr{स्पर्धक} (spardhak) — a contestant}

\label{lesson:MR-C530-spardhak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a trophy cup, then the Marathi for a sporting best.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{स्पर्धक}}
\textbf{\mr{स्पर्धक}} — \emph{spardhak} — \textquotedblleft{}a contestant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{या} \mr{स्पर्धेत} \mr{वीस} \mr{स्पर्धक} \mr{आहेत}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yā spardhet vīs spardhak āhet.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There are twenty contestants in this competition.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

Built on \mr{स्पर्धा}, a competition.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{स्पर्धक}} (\emph{spardhak}) is built on \mr{स्पर्धा}, \textquotedblleft{}a competition\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{spardhā}, \textquotedblleft{}rivalry\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the agent ending -\mr{क}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for a trophy cup, then the Marathi for a sporting best, then say \emph{spardhak} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{पटकावणे} (paṭkāvṇe)}{पटकावणे (paṭkāvṇe)}]{\mr{पटकावणे} (paṭkāvṇe) — to carry off; to win a prize}

\label{lesson:MR-C530-patkavne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a sporting best, then the Marathi for a contestant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{पटकावणे}}
\textbf{\mr{पटकावणे}} — \emph{paṭkāvṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to carry off; to win a prize\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mr{आमच्या} \mr{शाळेने} \mr{पहिलं} \mr{बक्षीस} \mr{पटकावलं}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmcyā śāḷene pahilaṁ bakṣīs paṭkāvlaṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our school carried off the first prize.
\end{quote}

Past, with -\mr{ने} (he …): \mr{त्याने} \mr{पदक} \mr{पटकावलं}, \emph{tyāne padak paṭkāvlaṁ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{पटकावणे}} (\emph{paṭkāvṇe}) is a Marathi verb for seizing a prize; its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmcyā śāḷene pahilaṁ bakṣīs paṭkāvlaṁ.} — Our school carried off the first prize.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for a sporting best, then the Marathi for a contestant, then say \emph{paṭkāvṇe} again
\end{itemize}
